STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no curved inner bowl wall. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, roughly 24 cm across.
b) Reference: the red sneaker at the left edge is partly out of frame, so no reliable count. The plate spans roughly 60% of the image height, and the wooden table slats/gaps give no clean scale. Trust the type cue.
Final width: about 24 cm, so area = 24 x 24 = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Rice: occupies about 30% of the plate (right half, a heaped mound). Footprint = 0.30 x 576 = 173 cm². Thickness: grains clump about 0.5 cm, stacked about 5-6 deep at the centre peak, so the average is about half the peak, roughly 2.5 cm. Volume = 173 x 2.5 = 432 ml. Density 0.8 g/ml gives 346 g. Rice is cooked white rice; kcal about 130 per 100 g.
- Carrots: about 6-7 cooked carrot pieces (glazed or roasted, each roughly 5-6 cm long, 1.5-2 cm thick), occupying about 12% of the plate, footprint about 69 cm². Stacked about 2 pieces deep, average thickness about 1.5 cm. Volume = 69 x 1.5 = 104 ml. Density 0.6 g/ml gives 62 g. Carrots cooked, about 40 kcal per 100 g (glazed may be a bit higher; use 40).

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible beyond the rice on the plate surface. Nothing else hidden.

STEP 5 - Totals:
- Rice: 346 g x 1.30 kcal/g = 450 kcal
- Carrots: 62 g x 0.40 kcal/g = 25 kcal
- Total: about 408 g, about 475 kcal.
